transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-06-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Jordan Reed (Redwood CSM), Rajiv Kapoor (FinEdge Eng Mgr), Maya Chen (FinEdge Lead Mobile), Derek Lau (FinEdge CTO)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this to 45, quick check-in on the SDK integration and the function calls for the payment reconciliation flow. How's it going on your side, Rajiv?

[00:32] Rajiv: Yeah thanks Samir. Overall it's moving, we've hooked up the Redwood SDK in our staging, the basic generation calls are fine. The issue we hit is when we use function_calling to get the structured payment object, sometimes the returned JSON is truncated or the keys are renamed, like amount -> amunt, and that breaks our downstream parser.

[01:05] Lina: Okay got it. A couple of quick clarifying things — are you using streaming responses or the non-streaming path? And are you setting the function_call param explicitly to the function name or using open-ended calling?

[01:22] Maya: We're using streaming because we wanted lower latency in mobile, and we set function_call to the function name. Might be related to streaming chunk boundaries.

[01:38] Lina: Streaming can split tokens across chunks which sometimes makes the transcriber reassemble imperfectly if your client doesn't buffer properly. For structured output we recommend either: (a) use non-streaming for the final call to ensure atomic JSON, or (b) implement a simple reassembly and validation step that rejects partial JSON until complete. Also you can use the SDK helper that does auto-reassembly — did you pull the latest SDK?

[02:05] Rajiv: We grabbed the npm from last week, let me check version... it's 0.9.1. Is there a patch?

[02:15] Lina: Yes please upgrade to 0.9.3 — we added the structured-output helper and improved streaming-chunk reassembly and retry for function_calling.

[02:30] Samir: I'll put the upgrade note in the follow-up along with sample payloads.

[02:36] Derek: Another thing we noticed is the model sometimes invents fields; our parser expects a strict schema. Any guidance on forcing strict schema adherence?

[02:48] Lina: Two levers — one is to use function_calling with a JSON schema in the function signature so the model must emit that shape. Second is Redwood's structured_output mode where you provide an output_schema and the runtime validates and can reject or retry generation if it doesn't match. Note, it's experimental in the hosted tier but available in the Dedicated sandbox.

[03:15] Rajiv: You said Dedicated sandbox — is that reachable for us in the POC? We really need determinism for the payment flow.

[03:23] Samir: For POC we can provision a short-lived dedicated pool in our staging region, it's typical. Lina, can you confirm resource availability?

[03:33] Lina: Yeah we can spin up a small Dedicated environment in us-west for testing. It'll be on a shared node but with isolated config for batch/quantization settings. Keep in mind dedicated will change cost profile and latency SLOs improve. Will need a quick onboarding ticket.

[03:50] Maya: That sounds good. One other blocker: encryption of PII. Do you have KMS integration? Our security team asked about customer-managed keys.

[04:02] Jordan: Yes we support KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption but if you need CMK we can wire a Dedicated or Private deployment. I'll attach the security doc in the follow-up.

[04:20] Rajiv: Great. Back to SDK — our mobile client is using the JS SDK through react-native, and we saw some weird tokenization mismatch where emoji in the payment description caused the schema to shift. Any recommendations?

[04:38] Lina: Normalize on the client — we recommend sanitizing or escaping special characters before sending. Also set the max_tokens and stop sequences in the SDK call; with structured output adding a clear end token helps. Example:
- call: client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-unified-1', messages, function_call: 'parse_payment', streaming: false, output_schema: {...}})

[05:05] Rajiv: Can you share that sample code? The current doc snippets are a bit generic.

[05:12] Samir: Yes I'll send a tailored snippet for react-native and the server side reconcilers. We'll include both streaming tips and non-streaming examples.

[05:28] Maya: On the server side, when we call the SDK function that triggers downstream reconciliation, sometimes the KV cache seems to return stale prefixes and causes doubled items in the reconciliation list — we think it's a cache issue.

[05:44] Lina: We have a few recommendations: tune the prefix cache TTL for your use case, and consider explicit cache invalidation after certain reconciliation windows. Also our runtime has a "strict-kv" flag for deterministic KV cache semantics in Dedicated. That said, I suspect what you saw is client-side dedup on retries. Are you using idempotency keys?

[06:08] Rajiv: We haven't implemented idempotency keys yet for retried function calls. That could explain duplicates.

[06:15] Lina: Add idempotency tokens on the request metadata; the SDK supports that out of the box. We'll add a code sample for that too.

[06:28] Derek: About latency — can you share rough numbers for structured output calls when streaming vs non-streaming? We need to decide trade-offs for mobile.

[06:38] Samir: Typical hosted numbers: non-streaming structured completion at 200-400ms for small payloads, streaming can drop tail latency near 100-200ms for initial tokens but total time may be similar. In Dedicated you get more consistent sub-100ms p50 for token generation depending on batch sizes. But this is workload dependent; we'll run a short E2E bench for your payload.

[07:03] Maya: Perfect, we'd like the bench to include our real sample payloads and simulate concurrent mobile clients.

[07:12] Samir: Noted. Lina — can you coordinate the bench and share the template?

[07:18] Lina: Yes I'll share a benchmark template and we'll run it in the Dedicated sandbox once they confirm. Please send the sample payloads and concurrency profile.

[07:27] Rajiv: We'll get that by Friday. Also our compliance folks want SOC 2 type II evidence and an audit log of API requests. Do you provide per-request audit logs?

[07:38] Jordan: Yes, audit logs are available in Dedicated and Private. Hosted provides limited logging for a shorter retention window, but for enterprise we can enable longer retention and integrate with your S3 or SIEM. I'll include the audit log appendix in the security doc.

[07:55] Derek: One final technical question, is there a recommended pattern to combine tool-calling with external DB lookups inside the function_call flow? We want the model to call a function that first validates an order against our DB, then returns structured output.

[08:12] Lina: Recommended pattern: use function_call to trigger a server-side lambda that does DB validation and returns a normalized object to the model if needed. Another approach is to pre-populate context with the DB result using ephemeral context so the model doesn't have to fetch. For strict correctness, prefer server-side validation as the source of truth. We'll share an architecture diagram.

[08:40] Samir: Great. To recap next steps: Samir sends SDK code snippets and upgrade note to 0.9.3; Lina provisions sandbox key and benchmark template; FinEdge shares sample payloads and concurrency profile by Friday; Jordan sends security doc & audit log details. We re-sync next Tuesday with bench results.

[09:05] Rajiv: Sounds good, thanks all.

[09:10] Maya: Thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround.

[09:15] Derek: Thanks.

[09:20] Samir: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with meeting notes and artifacts.

End of transcript.
